$comment: Gold queries against frozen-corpus.json. These back the CI regression guard. Add a fixture whenever a ranking behaviour is worth protecting; add it with known_miss when it records a failure the current ranking genuinely cannot satisfy.

queries.question: What is an agent harness?
queries.notes: Title match on the canonical wiki must outrank the supporting vault idea; knowledge tier is the reviewed answer.

queries.question: What is the best way to keep the quality of a long run from degrading?
queries.notes: Guards the stopword fix. Terms what/is/the/best/way/of/a/from match nothing meaningful; degrading and long run carry the signal. Before stopword filtering this query matched every document.

queries.question: How does model tiering work?
queries.notes: Guards punctuation trimming. Without it the token is `work?` and `tiering` still matches, but a query ending in the only meaningful term would retrieve nothing.

queries.question: Can sub-agents talk to each other directly?
queries.notes: Body-only match — the answer phrase peer-to-peer never appears in the title.

queries.question: How should execution bounds be enforced?
queries.notes: Scope filter must exclude vault:idea.harness-owns-execution-bounds despite it being the stronger lexical match.

queries.question: How should execution bounds be enforced?
queries.notes: Mirror of scope-knowledge-only; same question, opposite tier.

queries.question: least-privilege iam-roles
queries.notes: Tag-shaped query. Exercises tag scoring independent of title and body.

queries.question: What is the capital city of Portugal?
queries.notes: Nothing local should rank. Empty relevant set means recall is trivially satisfied; the value is precision@k, which must stay at 0. This is the regression guard for context pollution on out-of-domain questions.

queries.question: How do I combine lexical and semantic search results?
queries.notes: Document ranking succeeds here — the transcript is the only match and ranks first. The Phase 3 problem this fixture exists for is NOT ranking but snippet extraction: an early incidental match on `search results` anchors the snippet in the intro, so the passage that actually answers the question never reaches the model. Asserted separately in retrieval-eval.utils.test.ts; ranking metrics alone cannot see this failure.
